newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moldovan parliament authorises $100 mln Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan parliament authorises $100 mln Eurobond.

text.p: Moldova's parliament ratified on Wednesday an agreement between the Finance Ministry and U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch to issue a $100 million Eurobond.
The debut Eurobond will run for five years and pay annual interest of 9.5 to 9.7 percent.
"I hope the money will be in Moldova in June," Finance Minister Valeriu Chitan told Reuters.
He said the roadshow will take place from May 19 to May 30 in New York, Boston, Los Angeles, London, Zurich, Frankfurt and Paris.

Of the funds $75 million will be used to service Moldova's external debt, $15 million will be used as collateral for a 60 million lei ($13 million) National Bank loan to the Finance Ministry, and the rest will be used for current spending, mainly paying pensions and public-sector wages, Chitan said.
Including $570 million owed to Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, Moldova's external debt totals $1.2 billion -- about 60 percent of gross domestic product.
Up to 15 percent of the bond will be sold in the U.S. and the bulk will be placed in Europe, Chitan said.
Moldova will pay underwriting fees of 1.25 percent to Merrill Lynch, he added.

Merrill Lynch helped Moldova make a $30 million private placement last year, the first time the former Soviet republic tapped international capital markets. Those bonds mature in December 1999, paying annual interest of around 11 percent.
Moody's assigned Moldova a high speculative rating of Ba2 in January.

Victor Cibotari, deputy head of the finance ministry's Treasury department, said Germany's Dresdner Bank AG had proposed managing a further Eurobond for Moldova, and Japan's Daiwa Europe Ltd had proposed a Samurai issue, but these discussions were at an early stage. A Samurai bond is a yen issue raised in Japan by a foreign borrower.
